title: Blue Tern Logistics onboarding launch & connectivity handoff
summary: Kickoff to transition Blue Tern from evaluation to onboarding on Redwood Private. Reviewed network connectivity options (VPC peering vs private link), data residency/retention defaults, and initial pilot scope: routing inbound chat assist + embedding ops. Action items include security packet to Priya, pilot acceptance criteria, test dataset handoff, and scheduling an on-prem install window for the week of 10/26.
topics: network connectivity options (VPC peering, PrivateLink, IP allowlist)
data handling and retention / KMS integration
benchmarks and performance expectations (p95 latency targets)
transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-10-12
- Time: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 62 minutes (approx)
- Recording: enabled
- Notes: deck shared: tinyurl.com/redwood-btln-deck, security packet link: tinyurl.com/redwood-sec-pkt

Summary section (auto-gen, imperfect):
Maya: quick intro, set agenda. Luis covered onboarding milestones. Devon to own the install runbook. Customer asked about dedicated vs private; we clarified Redwood Private and on-prem bundle. Priya asked about KMS and audit logs. Tom asked about p95 latency and failover. Action items recorded at end.

Transcript body:
00:00 Maya (AE): okay hi everybody thanks for joining on time, i'm Maya with Redwood. appreciate you carving out the hour. uh quick round of intros?
00:08 Tom Wallace (CTO): yeah Tom here, CTO, Blue Tern. Sara's leading ML ops but i'm here for the infra side.
00:12 Sara Nguyen (Head of ML Ops): Sara, ML Ops. we'll mostly be hands on for the pilot.
00:16 Priya Rao (Security): Priya, security. I'll be looking at SSO, keys, and data retention.
00:18 Evan Cho (SRE): Evan, site reliability. we'll coordinate network.
00:21 Luis (CSM): great, I'm Luis, i'll run adoption milestones and track open tasks.
00:25 Devon (SE): Devon, Solutions Eng, i'll be your tech lead for the install and the benchmark work.
00:29 Maya: sweet. agenda: network connectivity options, security items, pilot success criteria, runbook and next steps. anything else to add?
00:36 Tom: maybe a quick peek at where we should place the model — we discusseddedicated earlier — want to confirm cost tradeoffs.
00:42 Maya: yep we'll cover routing and dedicated vs private trade offs.
01:05 Maya: (slides) first up connectivity. for Blue Tern's compliance needs we've got three common patterns: VPC peering, AWS PrivateLink, or on-prem install with direct routing. VPC peering is straightforward but requires route tables; PrivateLink can be easier for limiting network exposure.
01:25 Priya: when you say "PrivateLink" do we still see egress IPs from Redwood? we need predictable egress and per-call audit.
01:31 Devon: good question. for hosted PrivateLink the egress is from our managed connectors but you can require TLS mutual auth and we issue fixed egress ranges. audit logs are shipped to your SIEM via the console — we can toggle retention.
01:45 Priya: retention toggle—what's default? 30 days?
01:49 Luis: default on Private is 90 days, but we have enterprise retention packs and can configure to 365 under the compliance add-on. we'll note that in the security packet.
01:58 Priya: okay please send docs.
02:03 Maya: noted. action: send security packet.
02:07 Tom: on latency — our user-facing chat needs p95 under 350ms for short prompts, and embeddings for search are batched. is that achievable on Redwood Private?
02:17 Devon: p95 350 is tight but achievable if we pin a small-model variant on dedicated GPU pool and enable continuous batching thresholds. two levers: lower model size or move to dedicated reserved capacity. we ran similar with another logistics client using a quantized 7B.
02:37 Tom: ah okay uh how often do you see degrade at peak — like midday surges?
02:42 Devon: depends on workload shape. we recommend autoscaling buffer + a burst pool. we can set a policy to route to a fall-back cheaper variant when queue length exceeds threshold.
03:01 Evan: aside from that, what about KV cache — do you require server-side? we prefer not to leak session memory.
03:07 Devon: KV cache is optional; you can control TTL and whether it's persisted. note our runtime does prefix caching but you can disable per-route. i should warn, we saw some transcripts where the auto-transcription wrote K V cash so to be careful in notes.
03:21 (small laugh)
03:30 Priya: KMS — can we integrate with our AWS KMS? we need envelope encryption, separate key per env, and HSM backed keys if possible.
03:38 Maya: yes we support customer-managed keys. our Private and on-prem packages can use your KMS or HSM. we'll include configuration steps in the install runbook.
03:45 Priya: audit logs — will those include token-level cost breakouts? we need per-token accounting for billing and compliance.
03:52 Luis: token-level breakouts are available in the console; for Private we ship logs via S3/CloudWatch with structured fields you can ingest.
04:04 Sara: pilot scope — we agreed on two features: (1) internal agent for freight ops chat, (2) embedding-based search for manifests. timeline was 4 weeks?
04:12 Luis: correct, onboarding pilot 4 weeks: week 0 prep, week 1 deploy + smoke, week 2 integration, week 3 validation and acceptance.
04:20 Sara: acceptance criteria?
04:22 Maya: propose: pass functional tests (chat correctness > X on defined prompt set), p95 latency under 350ms for chat, embedding recall above baseline 0.78, and no critical security gaps.
04:35 Tom: can you define the prompt set baseline? we'll need time to label.
04:39 Luis: we'll share a template spreadsheet for evaluation prompts and expected outputs.
04:43 Devon: also we recommend 2 synthetic load tests: 50 RPS sustained and a 200 RPS 2-minute spike. that defines autoscale.
05:00 Evan: timing for on-prem install — if we want air-gapped, what's the lead time for shipping the bundle?
05:06 Devon: for the on-prem bundle typical lead is 2 weeks to prep artifacts, plus a 1–2 day install window. if you require additional QA images that's extra.
05:16 Priya: noted. for the pilot we'll try Private in your VPC first before full on-prem.
05:22 Maya: ok leaning Private first. next, runbook: Devon will own install steps, Luis will manage milestone tracking.
05:30 Devon: runbook outline: pre-checks (IAM roles, network routes, DNS), install (helm chart or binary), post-install smoke tests, perf bench script, rollback steps. i'll post the full markdown runbook to the shared drive.
05:46 Sara: can you include sample manifests for the embedding pipeline? we have some custom preproc.
05:51 Devon: yes, we'll include sample dockerfiles and a sample preprocessing step.
06:00 (silence while note taking)
06:18 Priya: about SSO — we use Okta, SAML. support for SCIM?
06:24 Luis: yes SAML SSO works for console access. SCIM provisioning is supported via our enterprise connector. will include scim guide.
06:31 Priya: perfect. any SOC2 artifacts?
06:33 Maya: yes SOC2 type II report is in the security packet.
06:37 Priya: please redact vendor names if possible.
06:40 Luis: we provide a redacted version for procurement, full for legal under NDA.
06:45 Tom: procurement — who signs the pilot MSA?
06:48 Luis: pilot MSA is a lightweight agreement; legal can sign it. we'll send a templated MSA and a statement of work for the pilot.
06:55 Tom: great.
07:05 Maya: ok big picture timeline — target pilot start week of 10/26, staging deploy during week 1, integration week 2, acceptance week 4. any major blockers?
07:14 Sara: we'll need the eval prompt template and the benchmark harness. also need a test dataset sanitized for PII.
07:20 Maya: we can supply a sanitized sample and the template. action.
07:24 Devon: technical note: if you plan to use quantized models to save GPU memory, we may need to validate output quality on your prompts. that's typically an EOD for us — we'll run a small quality sweep.
07:37 Evan: on the networking piece — our infra team prefers PrivateLink over peering due to cross-account constraints. how long to configure?
07:43 Devon: configuration is usually a day of networking work + verification, we'll pair with Evan for that.
07:49 Evan: i'll share a contact for our networking engineer.
07:51 Maya: good. next section: troubleshooting and support. Luis: outline support SLAs and escalation matrix.
07:58 Luis: pilot includes business hours support with a dedicated Slack channel. Dedicated and Private enterprise tiers have 24/7 on-call. we'll set up the Slack channel and paging policy if we go to production.
08:10 Priya: also need audit webhook to our SIEM for any admin changes.
08:15 Devon: we can configure admin-change webhook and send to your collector endpoint.
08:19 Priya: what's the window for changing retention? we need to ensure immutability for 90 days for audit.
08:25 Luis: retention changes are something we can set in provisioning; once set it's enforced by policy.
08:29 (crosstalk: agreement)
08:40 Maya: recapping next steps verbally before we close.
08:43 Maya: Action items: 1) Redwood send security packet and SOC2 redacted (owner: Maya / due: 2026-10-14), 2) share evaluation prompt template and bench harness (owner: Luis / due: 2026-10-15), 3) schedule VPC/PrivateLink pairing session with Evan and Devon (owner: Devon / due: 2026-10-16), 4) Blue Tern to share sanitized test dataset and contact for network engineer (owner: Sara / due: 2026-10-16), 5) draft pilot MSA and SOW for review (owner: Luis / due: 2026-10-15).
09:14 Tom: can you add a note about fall-back policy for when dedicated pool is saturated?
09:18 Devon: yes will include routing policy sample.
09:22 Maya: last Qs?
09:25 Priya: one small thing — do you support logging PII redaction at ingestion?
09:30 Devon: ingestion redaction is available as a pre-processor, but for Private we recommend doing PII redaction on your side before sending. we'll include examples.
09:41 Maya: ok thanks everyone. i'll send meeting notes and the packet.
09:45 Luis: i'll create the Jira epic and invite all for the pairing session.
09:50 Sara: thanks all. excited to get started.
09:54 Maya: great, meeting adjourned.
